result.summary: Reviewed git diff main...HEAD for lib/letflow/dlq/entry.ex (the only production code file changed; lib/letflow/dlq.ex confirmed genuinely untouched by the diff), the design doc, the ISSUE record, and the ELIXIR-DEV handoff. invariant_assessment.detail: (a) All reads/writes of Entry still go through Letflow.Dlq's Repo calls, each passed prefix: prefix from opts -- unchanged by this diff, confirmed by re-reading dlq.ex's enqueue/2 (untouched). (b) No migration touched by this diff -- dlq_entries' schema-per-tenant placement is pre-existing and out of scope for this fix. (c) tenant_id derivation: enqueue/2 (the sole caller) still derives tenant_id from opts[:prefix] via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 and Map.merges it into insert_attrs -- entirely unchanged by this diff. The changed line inside insert_changeset/2 (put_change(:tenant_id, Map.get(attrs, :tenant_id)) instead of cast(attrs, [:tenant_id, ...])) reads the exact same insert_attrs map enqueue/2 already builds; it does not add or remove any path by which a caller-supplied tenant_id could reach the row beyond what already existed pre-fix. No new caller of insert_changeset/2 was introduced. 0003's addendum (derived-from-prefix, not caller-supplied) remains satisfied by enqueue/2's unchanged Map.take/2 allowlist + Map.merge/2, which is the actual enforcement boundary -- exactly as the issue itself documents.

result.vulnerability_closure_analysis: Re-read the issue's own actual scope (docs/issues/ISS-0381.yaml, description + candidate_scope_for_whoever_picks_this_up) before judging what property this fix must deliver. The issue is explicitly an idiom-gap / docstring-vs-implementation contradiction, NOT a claim that a caller-supplied tenant_id can currently reach the DB (the issue's own description states plainly: 'Today this is harmless ... no caller-supplied value for any of these five fields can currently reach insert_changeset/2' -- enqueue/2's Map.take/2 is the real, and only, current enforcement boundary). The issue's candidate_scope explicitly prescribes put_change/3 reading attrs as the correct fix mechanism for tenant_id/created_at, stating outright: 'only the mechanism changes from cast to put_change, not the caller contract.' The design doc and the shipped docstring both plainly disclose that put_change(:tenant_id, Map.get(attrs, :tenant_id)) still reads the same attrs map -- so a caller who bypasses enqueue/2 and calls insert_changeset/2 directly with a raw/unfiltered attrs map still has tenant_id/created_at influenced by whatever that raw map contains, identical to pre-fix behavior for those two fields. This is NOT a regression and NOT a false claim: the property this fix actually delivers, correctly, is (1) status/retry_count/retry_history can no longer be influenced via cast/3 under any attrs content -- they now hard-depend on Ecto.Schema struct defaults, closing that sub-slice completely regardless of caller discipline; and (2) the changeset's structure now genuinely matches its own docstring's description of the enforcement mechanism, rather than silently relying on caller (enqueue/2) discipline while claiming otherwise. Testing this fix against 'no caller-supplied tenant_id can ever influence the row' would be testing a property this fix never claimed and the issue never asked for -- the actual, correctly-scoped and correctly-delivered property is 'the changeset now correctly enforces what its docstring already claimed, for the 3 fields that have safe schema defaults; for tenant_id/created_at the caller-discipline boundary (enqueue/2's Map.take/2) remains the real enforcement, exactly as before and exactly as the issue's own text states.' No cross-tenant leak is introduced: enqueue/2, the sole caller, is untouched and continues to derive tenant_id from opts[:prefix], never from raw request attrs.
result.default_correctness_check: Verified against the Ecto.Schema field definitions in entry.ex (schema block): field(:retry_history, {:array, :map}, default: []), field(:retry_count, :integer, default: 0), field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [...], default: :pending). Since %Entry{} is built as a fresh struct literal in Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2 before insert_changeset/2 is called, these three fields carry their correct Ecto.Schema struct defaults on `entry.data` even though cast/3 no longer touches them -- no silent-nil regression. Confirmed independently by ELIXIR-DEV's own reported observation of the actual logged INSERT SQL during the enqueue/2 happy-path test: INSERT INTO dlq_entries (status, tenant_id, created_at, entry_type, retry_count, retry_history, id) VALUES (...) [:pending, <tenant_id>, <created_at>, "event", 0, [], <id>] -- every previously-cast-now-defaulted-or-put_change field lands correctly end-to-end.
result.validate_required_nil_check: Confirmed against Ecto.Changeset semantics: validate_required/2 calls Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2 internally, which checks :changes first, falling back to :data only when the field has no entry in :changes. put_change(:tenant_id, nil) DOES add a :tenant_id => nil entry to :changes (put_change/3 always writes to :changes regardless of value, including nil), so get_field/2 returns nil from :changes (does not fall back to :data), and validate_required/2 treats nil as missing and adds the 'can't be blank' error -- exactly as the design and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR claimed. This is different from status/retry_count's omission-from-cast case, where no :changes entry exists at all and get_field/2 correctly falls back to :data's schema-default value -- the two behaviors are not the same mechanism and the design/docstring correctly distinguish them.
